subject: springboot
question: Which annotation selects a specific bean by name at an injection point when several beans share a type?
options: @Profile
@Qualifier
@Order
@Lazy
explanation: @Qualifier narrows autowiring candidates to the bean with the matching qualifier or name.

subject: springboot
question: Since Spring 4.3, when can @Autowired be omitted on a constructor?
options: When the class is declared final
When the constructor is private
When the bean has prototype scope
When the class declares exactly one constructor
explanation: If a bean class has a single constructor, Spring uses it for injection automatically without @Autowired.

subject: springboot
question: What is the default scope of a Spring bean?
options: prototype
request
session
singleton
explanation: Unless specified otherwise, the container creates one shared instance per bean definition, which is singleton scope.

subject: springboot
question: Which injection style does the Spring team recommend for mandatory dependencies?
options: Setter injection
Field injection
Constructor injection
Lookup method injection
explanation: Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit, allows final fields, and guarantees the object is fully initialized.

subject: springboot
question: How can a bean receive every bean that implements a NotificationSender interface?
options: Inject a single NotificationSender with @Primary
Inject the ApplicationContext and call getBean(NotificationSender.class)
Annotate the interface with @Bean
Inject a List<NotificationSender>
explanation: Spring injects all matching beans into a collection-typed injection point, ordered by @Order or Ordered when present.

subject: springboot
question: What does placing @Lazy on a constructor parameter do?
options: Injects a proxy that resolves the real bean on first use
Makes the bean prototype-scoped
Skips injection if the bean is missing
Delays the whole application startup until first request
explanation: @Lazy at an injection point injects a lazy-resolution proxy, which also helps break circular dependencies.

subject: springboot
question: Two beans of type PaymentClient exist; one is marked @Primary and the injection point uses @Qualifier("backupClient"). Which bean is injected?
options: The @Primary bean
Whichever bean was registered first
Neither; startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException
The bean named backupClient
explanation: An explicit @Qualifier at the injection point takes precedence over @Primary.

subject: springboot
question: What is ObjectProvider<T> useful for at an injection point?
options: Lazily or optionally obtaining a bean, e.g. with getIfAvailable()
Registering new bean definitions at runtime
Converting a bean into a different type
Forcing a singleton to become a prototype
explanation: ObjectProvider allows deferred, optional or unique-if-available retrieval without failing at startup.

subject: springboot
question: Why is a @PreDestroy method on a prototype-scoped bean never called by the container?
options: The container does not manage prototype beans after handing them out
Prototype beans are destroyed only on JVM exit
@PreDestroy is supported only on @Configuration classes
Prototype beans are always wrapped in proxies that swallow callbacks
explanation: Spring configures and returns prototypes but does not track them, so the client is responsible for cleanup.

subject: springboot
question: A singleton bean receives a prototype bean through its constructor. What does it get each time it uses that field?
options: The same prototype instance, created once at injection time
A proxy that creates a new instance per call by default
null after the first use
A fresh prototype instance on every method call
explanation: Injection happens once; use ObjectProvider, @Lookup or a scoped proxy to get a new prototype each time.

subject: springboot
question: In what order are these initialization callbacks invoked for a bean?
options: Custom init method, then @PostConstruct, then afterPropertiesSet()
afterPropertiesSet(), then @PostConstruct, then the custom init method
@PostConstruct, then afterPropertiesSet(), then the custom init method
@PostConstruct, then the custom init method, then afterPropertiesSet()
explanation: Annotation callbacks run first, then InitializingBean, then the init method declared on the bean definition.

subject: springboot
question: In @Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false), what happens when beanA() calls beanB() directly?
options: The container's singleton beanB is returned via CGLIB
Startup fails because inter-bean calls are forbidden
A new instance is created by a plain Java call, not the container's singleton
beanB becomes prototype-scoped automatically
explanation: Without CGLIB proxying, @Bean methods are ordinary methods, so inter-bean calls bypass the container.
